title: Investigate slice-dependent quality regressions after FP8/INT8 quantization for reranker models
creator: Anil Kapoor
description: Recent FP8 and INT8 profile candidates reduced average token compute but produced non-uniform ranking quality regressions on specific query slices (long queries, personalized signals, numeric-heavy queries). This ticket scopes a focused benchmark and calibration workflow to identify which model components / data slices drive NDCG and MRR degradation and produce gating thresholds and mitigations for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Clear attribution: map quality delta (NDCG@10, MRR@10) to a small set of quantization levers (per-layer scale, outlier clipping, per-head sensitivity)
A reproducible calibration workflow that reduces worst-case slice regression to within defined SLAs (<=0.5% NDCG relative drop for high-impact slices)
Automated evaluation job(s) that generate per-slice NDCG/MRR reports and significance tests suitable for gating in the CI pipeline
Rollback and fallback documented: documented fallback to fp16/int16 variant and shadow-canary gating steps
evaluation_plan: Dataset: curated evaluation corpus of 200k labeled query->candidate pairs (production distribution + amplified long-tail slices)
Primary metrics: NDCG@10, MRR@10 computed per-slice and overall; report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals
Slices: length buckets (<=16, 17-64, >64 tokens), personalization signal present/absent, numeric-heavy, sparse-history users, rare tokens (tail 1%)
Statistical gating: require p-value < 0.05 for observed improvements; for regressions use bootstrap to compute CI and require worst-case slice drop <= 0.5% absolute NDCG or <=0.7% MRR
Staging: run shadow-serving A/B on 48h of live traffic for top 10k queries to validate real-world ranking differences before canary rollout
calibration_workflow: Offline activation analysis: collect activation histograms per layer/head using representative corpus; flag heavy-tail layers for per-channel scaling
Per-layer scale search: grid search for symmetric/asymmetric scales with KL and MSE objectives on 5k heldout examples
KL-based outlier clipping: test 0.01/0.05/0.1 percentiles to control saturation in attention projections
Hybrid profile approach: allow FP8 for attention+mlp but INT8 for embedding/softmax to preserve rank probabilities
Quant-aware fine-tuning (QAT) plan: small-budget QAT on 100M tokens for top candidate profile if calibration alone fails
benchmarking_tasks: Implement per-slice NDCG/MRR exporter in eval harness (adds per-request metadata tagging and provenance)
Add head/layer sensitivity profiler that reports expected rank-signal loss when quantized
Run full sweep across candidate profiles: legacy-fp16 baseline, fp8-global, fp8-hybrid, int8-symmetric, int8-perchannel
Aggregate compute: report latency/throughput delta and estimated token cost savings for each profile
rollback_plan: If any high-impact slice shows NDCG drop >0.8% absolute during canary, abort rollout and switch to fp16 baseline
Automated fallback route in runtime: route failing queries by slice label to fp16/int16 model variant for 1 hour while we investigate
Postmortem: capture inputs causing largest per-query score deltas and persist to /data/quant-investigations for debug
updates: 2025-02-15 - Created ticket: baseline reproduction shows avg NDCG drop 0.15% but >1.2% on long queries (>64 tokens). Initial owner assigned (Maya).
2025-02-18 - Ran per-layer activation collector on representative corpus (30k samples). Layer 9 feed-forward showed heavy-tail activations; flagged for per-channel scaling.

2025-02-22 - First calibration sweep completed: fp8-hybrid with attention in FP8 and softmax in INT8 reduced long-query NDCG drop to 0.6%; increased tail MRR variance. Uploaded sweep artifacts to Drive.
2025-02-26 - Design/PM review: agreed to add shadow-serving test and expand slice definitions to include personalization signal. PR for eval exporter opened (see artifacts).
2025-03-02 - Began 48h shadow-serving with fp8-hybrid profile on 10k top queries. Early signs: latency down 18%, cost down ~12%, long-query NDCG at 0.52% drop (inside gating target but borderline).

test_results_summary: Offline sweep (all slices): overall NDCG drop vs fp16 = 0.14% (95% CI [0.10,0.18])
Long-query slice (>64 tokens): NDCG drop = 0.52% (95% CI [0.40,0.68]) for fp8-hybrid
Personalization-on slice: MRR change = -0.25% (not significant, p=0.12)
Latency: fp8-hybrid median tail latency -18% vs fp16; throughput +22%
next_steps: Complete 48h shadow serving and collect per-query deltas for top regressions
Run targeted per-channel INT8 experiment on Layer 9 and measure slice impact
If shadow results remain within gating, open canary rollout plan with SRE and PM signoff
Prepare CI gating jobs that fail the PR if any slice regresses beyond acceptance thresholds
notes: This ticket intentionally separates overall average metrics from slice-level worst-case checks to avoid masking regressions.
We should coordinate with console team to expose per-slice NDCG charts in runtime-1.22 release dashboards.
Keep calibration notebooks idempotent and track random seeds for reproducibility.
